experiencias.tituloListado: Cacao and bird tours in Cubarral, Colombia
experiencias.metaDescripcion: Cacao tours, birdwatching and group visits at the Vuelo Carmesí agroecological farm in Cubarral, Meta (Colombia). Duration, group size and price in Colombian pesos for each experience.

origen.texto: You meet the cacao from the moment it is born on the tree. 1,300 traceable plants, 12 native varieties, and a process you can follow with your own eyes.

sostenible.texto: Agroecological management and Good Agricultural Practices in every corner. Every harvest respects the soil, the water and the farm's natural cycles.

artesanal.texto: You don't read about the process: you watch it. From box fermentation to grinding, every step from bean to bar happens in front of you.

biodiversidad.texto: You walk through a living ecosystem where plants and wildlife are cared for as the heart of the business, not as decoration.

autenticas.texto: Farming, environmental education and hands-on tourism in a single visit that truly connects you to this land.

seguro.texto: A specialist guide on every outing, assistance insurance, and small groups so you can enjoy it without crowds or rushing.

pruebaSocial.titulo: Hundreds of people have already trusted us
pruebaSocial.bajada: Since 2023, institutions, organizations and families have chosen Vuelo Carmesí to experience cacao from the root up.
pruebaSocial.organizaciones: Organizations that have visited our farm

sobreNosotros.titulo: A project born from the land
sobreNosotros.texto: We are an agroecological project devoted to growing and transforming cacao, where we champion practices that respect the land and turn every harvest into an experience that connects people to it. Every visit is a flight for the senses: the aroma of cacao mid-transformation, the sound of the farm at dawn, and the taste of chocolate made in the very place the cacao grows.
sobreNosotros.texto2: Every visit is a flight for the senses: the smell of ripe cacao, the sound of the farm at dawn, and the taste of chocolate made exactly where the cacao grew.

certificaciones.titulo: Backed by those who look after the land
certificaciones.bajada: Our agroecological and tourism practices are backed by official bodies. We work transparently, making every process part of the experience.

aviturismoAviso.texto: 180 species recorded on a public eBird hotspot, the migration window — October to April — and who leads the outing.

aviturismo.h1: Birding in Cubarral, Meta: 180 species among shade-grown cacao
aviturismo.lead: 180 species recorded at a public eBird hotspot, on 1.2 hectares of agroecological farmland between 600 and 850 m above sea level. You do not have to take our word for it: the list is published and anyone can check it before writing to us.
aviturismo.ebirdTexto: The hotspot is published on eBird as Vuelo Carmesí. It is the complete list, maintained by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology platform, and you can consult and verify it without asking us.

resumen.especies: recorded at the hotspot, with a public eBird list
resumen.altura: above sea level, foothills between the Llanos and Sumapaz
resumen.franja: the peak activity window, every day of the year

residentes.texto: The seven photographed on the farm. None is endemic to Colombia: what they offer is reliability, not rarity. The rest of the 180 are on the eBird list.

migratoriasCard.texto: They come down from the northern hemisphere to winter here and join the list for those seven months. That is why the date of your visit matters.

alta.nota: The residents plus the boreal migrants that come down from the north. This is the window international birders look for.

baja.nota: The species listed above are just as visible: they are here year-round and do not depend on the season.

franja.nota: Activity drops once the sun is high. The walk starts before dawn to make the most of it.

salida.que: Departure with binoculars from the meeting point

amanecer.que: Walk through wildlife corridors and shade-grown cacao

recorrido.nota: Groups of 2 to 8, basic to intermediate birding level. Booking and current rates are on the <ficha>experience page</ficha>.

faq.p1: Can you host a group of 40 people on the same day?
faq.r1: Yes. Large groups are handled by rotating subgroups, each with its own guide, so nobody does the tour in a group of forty. Write to us with the exact number and we will confirm availability for the date you need.
faq.p2: Can a bus reach the farm?
faq.r2: Yes. The road is paved all the way to the farm and any vehicle can reach it, including buses and vans. The car park has room for 4 cars and 1 bus.
faq.r3: The visit goes ahead: the tour is outdoors but there are covered areas for the cacao processing, the snack and the chocotherapy. That is why we ask the group to bring a rain jacket or poncho.
faq.p4: Do you invoice in the school's or company's name?
faq.r4: Yes. Tick the invoicing box on the form and include the tax ID: the quote comes with the tax details your procurement team needs.
faq.r5: Every visit includes accident and assistance insurance for each participant. If your institution needs the cover detailed in writing, we send it with the quote.
faq.p6: How far in advance should we book?
faq.r6: A booking is confirmed with the payment receipt and a minimum notice period. For large groups it is worth getting in touch earlier, because exclusive dates are scheduled in order of confirmation.
faq.r7: Yes, as an add-on. The country lunch is not included in any plan and is quoted by group size.
faq.p8: Can birdwatching be combined with the cacao experience?
faq.r8: Yes, that is the full-day plan: birdwatching starts at dawn and the cacao experience runs through the morning, with breakfast and a snack on the same day.

ninez.titulo: Our commitment to children and adolescents
ninez.intro: Finca Agroturística Vuelo Carmesí is committed to the full protection of children and adolescents and rejects any form of Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children and Adolescents (ESCNNA). In compliance with Law 679 of 2001 and Law 1336 of 2009, the establishment adopts preventive, control and protective measures against any situation that violates the rights of minors in the context of tourism services.
ninez.ingreso1: Minors may not enter or remain on the premises without meeting the legal requirements established by Colombian law.
ninez.ingreso2: Every minor must be accompanied by a parent, legal guardian or duly authorised adult, presenting the required documentation at check-in.
ninez.ingreso3: When a minor takes part in activities, events, tours or services without a parent or legal guardian present, they must provide written authorisation signed by them.
ninez.auto1: Full name and identification of the minor.
ninez.auto2: Name and identification of the responsible adult accompanying them.
ninez.auto3: Dates of the activity or contracted service.
ninez.auto4: Contact details of the parents or legal guardians.
ninez.autoNota: The establishment may request copies of identity documents and, where it deems necessary, an authorisation notarised before a notary public.
ninez.control1: The farm reserves the right to refuse entry or service when the authorisation is not adequately proven or where there are indications that could compromise the safety, wellbeing or protection of the minor.
ninez.control2: It reserves the right of admission and will report to the competent authorities any suspicious conduct related to the exploitation, abuse or violation of the rights of children and adolescents.
ninez.compromisoTexto: Finca Agroturística Vuelo Carmesí promotes responsible, safe tourism committed to the full protection of children and adolescents.

cancelacion.metaDescripcion: Booking, cancellation and payment terms for Vuelo Carmesí experiences.

completo.cuando: Cancellation within 24 hours of booking and more than 15 days in advance

medio.cuando: Between 15 and 7 days before the activity
medio.que: 30% penalty on the total amount paid

cancelacion.reserva1: All activities must be booked in advance and paid in full before they take place.
cancelacion.reserva2: Online bookings must be confirmed at least 48 hours in advance by sending proof of payment through the channels authorised by the farm.
cancelacion.reserva3: Quotes are for information only and do not constitute a booking confirmation. All bookings are subject to availability.
cancelacion.reserva4: Once a booking is confirmed, any change of date, activity or itinerary is subject to availability and to the terms of the contracted service.
cancelacion.reserva5: Visitors must provide truthful and complete information, including names, identification documents and any other data required to comply with current regulations.
cancelacion.pago1: On booking, 30% of the service value is paid; the remaining 70% is paid in cash on the day of the activity.
cancelacion.pago2: Payment is made by bank transfer to the farm's authorised account, or via NEQUI and BreB. Write to us and we will send you the details.
cancelacion.visitante1: Penalties for changes or cancellations apply only once the booking has been confirmed.
cancelacion.visitante2: To cancel, message us on WhatsApp or at the contact email, stating the name the booking was made under and the date.
cancelacion.repro1: Anyone who does not show up or arrives after the set time forfeits their place and the booking is cancelled.
cancelacion.repro2: Rescheduling is possible only if there is availability and by prior agreement between the parties. Any change of date, activity, itinerary or refund is subject to the terms of the contracted service and to existing availability.
cancelacion.finca1: Finca Agroturística Vuelo Carmesí will make every reasonable effort to keep to the established schedule. Times may be changed for reasons of force majeure, safety or extraordinary circumstances beyond its control, without this giving rise to liability for the company.
cancelacion.finca2: If we have to move your experience for any of those reasons, we will contact you to agree a new date subject to availability.
cancelacion.finca3: Birdwatching is not cancelled for lack of sightings: observing wildlife can never be guaranteed, and the guided walk goes ahead regardless.

datos.metaDescripcion: What personal data Vuelo Carmesí collects through the forms on this site, what it is used for, how long it is kept and how to exercise your rights under Colombian Law 1581 of 2012.
datos.responsable: Finca Agroturística Vuelo Carmesí, located at {direccion}, is the controller of the personal data collected through this site. For anything related to this document —including exercising your rights— write to {email} or call {telefono}.
datos.d1: Contact form: your name, your email address and the message you write.
datos.d2: Experience booking: your name, email, phone number, number of people, the date and time you choose and any notes you add.
datos.d3: Shop order: your name, email, phone number, address, city and postal code, together with the products and quantities you ordered.
datos.d4: Group enquiry: the type of institution, its name and tax ID if you give it to us, the name and role of the person writing, email, phone number, number of people, ages, tentative date and anything else you want to tell us.
datos.datosNota: We do not ask for sensitive data —health, ethnic origin, beliefs, biometrics— or financial data. Nothing is charged online on this site: we will never ask you for a card number.
datos.f1: Answering your message, your booking request or your enquiry.
datos.f2: Confirming, coordinating and delivering the experience you booked, or preparing and shipping the order you placed.
datos.f3: Sending you the operational emails: confirmation, status changes and cancellation of your booking or order.
datos.f4: Meeting our obligations as a registered tourism provider: visitor records, National Tourism Registry requirements and child protection rules.
datos.f5: Keeping internal records of bookings, orders and enquiries, and the accounting and tax supporting documents required by law.
datos.finalidadesNota: We do not use your data for advertising and we do not add you to any mailing list. If we ever want to write to you about something other than your booking or your order, we will ask you separately.
datos.a1: By submitting any of the forms on this site you give us prior, express and informed authorisation to process the data you entered, for the purposes set out in this document and no others.
datos.a2: Giving it is voluntary, but without it we cannot provide the service: there is no way to confirm a booking without your name and phone number, or to ship an order without your address.
datos.a3: You can withdraw it at any time by writing to us. Withdrawal does not cover data we must keep while a legal or contractual obligation is still in force —for example, the supporting document for a sale already invoiced.
datos.r1: To know, update and correct your data.
datos.r2: To ask for proof of the authorisation you gave us.
datos.r3: To be told what use we have made of them.
datos.r4: To access your data free of charge.
datos.r5: To withdraw your authorisation or ask us to delete your data, where no legal or contractual duty requires us to keep them.
datos.r6: To file complaints with the Superintendency of Industry and Commerce for breaches of the law.
datos.c1: The channel is {email}. Write from the address you contacted us with, tell us what you need —to know, update, correct, delete or withdraw— and, if it is a correction, what the correct value is.
datos.c2: An enquiry is answered within ten business days at most. If we cannot, we tell you why and resolve it within the following five business days.
datos.c3: A complaint is handled within fifteen business days at most, counted from the day after we receive it. If we cannot, we tell you why and when we will resolve it, within the following eight business days.
datos.c4: If a complaint arrives incomplete, we tell you within five days so you can complete it. If two months go by without a reply from you, we understand you have withdrawn it.
datos.canalNota: The law requires you to go through this process with us before filing a complaint with the Superintendency of Industry and Commerce.
datos.conservacionTitulo: How long we keep them, and where
datos.cs1: We keep them for as long as our relationship with you lasts and, afterwards, for as long as the legal, accounting and tax obligations arising from your booking or order remain in force. Once there is no reason to keep them, they are deleted.
datos.cs2: The information lives in a database and on servers of infrastructure providers located in the United States: the site on Vercel, the server on Render and the database on Neon. Operational emails are sent through Google's email service and internal alerts reach the team through Telegram. By authorising the processing you also authorise that international transfer.
datos.cs3: Those providers act as processors: they handle the data on our behalf and for the purposes of this document. We do not sell your data, we do not share it for advertising purposes and we do not hand it to third parties, unless a competent authority requires it.
datos.cs4: The panel where bookings, orders and enquiries are managed is password protected and used only by the team members who handle that work.
datos.m1: The forms on this site are meant for adults. When a booking includes minors, their data is provided by the responsible adult, who is the one authorising its processing.
datos.m2: Data of minors is processed only when it serves their best interests and respects their fundamental rights. Entry requirements and what a minor's authorisation must contain are set out in the child protection policy.
datos.k1: This site uses no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies. No third party is measuring where you browse.
datos.k2: The only thing stored in your browser is technical: the shop cart and your last order, in your device's local storage, so you do not lose what you added if you reload the page. It does not leave your browser until you confirm the order, and you can clear it by emptying the cart or clearing the site's data.
datos.k3: The admin panel uses a session cookie, but it is only created when a team member logs in. Nothing is installed for someone visiting the site.

tienda.metaDescripcion: Terms of sale for the Vuelo Carmesí shop: how an order is placed, prices, payment methods, shipping, right of withdrawal, payment reversal and legal warranty.
tienda.aviso: Confirming an order in the shop is not a payment: it is a request. We check stock, write to you to agree on the payment method and shipping, and only then is the purchase final. Until that moment nothing is charged and you can walk away at no cost.
tienda.v1: The products in this shop are sold by Finca Agroturística Vuelo Carmesí, a tourism provider listed in the National Tourism Registry under number 179868, located at {direccion}.
tienda.v2: For anything about your order, the channel is {email} or {telefono}.
tienda.v3: These terms apply to shop products. Experiences at the farm have their own booking, payment and cancellation rules.
tienda.p1: You add products to the cart and fill in the checkout form with your contact and delivery details.
tienda.p2: On confirming, you get an email with what you ordered. That email acknowledges the request; it is not yet acceptance of the purchase.
tienda.p3: We check stock and write to you to agree on the payment method and shipping.
tienda.p4: The purchase is complete once we confirm your order and agree payment and shipping with you. Delivery and warranty periods run from there.
tienda.pedidoNota: If a product sells out between your order and our check, we tell you and refund whatever you paid for it at no cost. You can swap it for something else or cancel the order.
tienda.pr1: Prices are in Colombian pesos and include VAT.
tienda.pr2: Shipping is not included in the price: it is quoted separately depending on the destination city and confirmed before we ship.
tienda.pr3: The price that counts is the one shown in the shop when you placed the order. A later change does not affect you.
tienda.pr4: The stock shown on a product page is the stock at the moment the page loaded. A product may sell out while you complete the order.
tienda.pr5: If we spot an obvious error in a price or a description, we tell you before charging anything and you can cancel the order at no cost.
tienda.pa1: Nothing is charged online. The site does not take card payments or store financial data, and it will never ask you for a card number.
tienda.pa2: Payment is agreed when we confirm the order: bank transfer to the farm's account, Nequi or BreB. We send you the details through the same channel we are talking on.
tienda.pa3: Any message asking you to pay into an account other than the one we confirmed through our own channels does not come from us. When in doubt, write to us before transferring.
tienda.e1: We ship within Colombia. The shipping method, cost and delivery time depend on the destination city and are agreed with you before we ship.
tienda.e2: The delivery period starts when payment is confirmed, not when you submit the form.
tienda.e3: You enter the delivery address at checkout. If it is incomplete or wrong and the parcel comes back, the second shipment has a cost.
tienda.e4: On delivery, check the packaging in front of the courier. If it arrives torn or opened, note it on the delivery slip and write to us the same day.
tienda.re1: You exercise the right of withdrawal by writing to {email} within the deadline and returning the product in the same condition you received it. Return shipping is at your expense, as the law provides; the rest of the money is refunded in full.
tienda.re2: The law excludes from withdrawal goods that by their nature deteriorate or expire quickly, and goods made to your specification. Almost everything we sell is food —chocolate and cacao— so once shipped, a perishable product is outside the right of withdrawal. It is still covered by the warranty, which is what protects you if it arrives in poor condition.
tienda.re3: Legal warranty: if the product arrives defective, incomplete, expired or is not what you ordered, write to us with photos as soon as you receive it and we replace it or refund you, as you choose under the law. For food, the warranty period is the expiry date printed on the product.
tienda.re4: Payment reversal applies when the purchase was paid by card or another electronic payment instrument and there was fraud, an unrequested transaction, an undelivered product or a defective one. You request it from your bank or the payment issuer, and we support the process with the order records.
tienda.rc1: The channel for any claim is {email}. We reply within fifteen business days.
tienda.rc2: If you are not satisfied, you can turn to the Superintendency of Industry and Commerce, Colombia's consumer protection authority.
tienda.rc3: These terms are governed by Colombian law, in particular Law 1480 of 2011 —the Consumer Statute— and the rules on e-commerce and distance selling.
tienda.da1: The data you enter at checkout is used to ship your order and to send the operational emails, and nothing else. What we collect, how long we keep it and how to ask us to correct or delete it is set out in the personal data policy.

sostenibilidad.metaDescripcion: Sustainability policy of Finca Agroturística Vuelo Carmesí: environmental, sociocultural and economic commitments of the provider, under Colombia's Sustainable Tourism Sectoral Standards.
sostenibilidad.compromiso: Finca Agroturística Vuelo Carmesí is a family cacao farm in Cubarral, Meta, that opened its doors to tourism. We commit to making sure that receiving visitors never works against what makes the farm possible: the soil, the water, the forest and the people who work it. This policy sets out that commitment across the three areas of Colombia's Sustainable Tourism Sectoral Standards —environmental, sociocultural and economic—, applies to all our experiences and binds the whole team.
sostenibilidad.am1: Growing without agrochemicals, with agroecological management and Good Agricultural Practices certified by the ICA.
sostenibilidad.am2: Conserving the farm's native species and the genetic material of the region's cacao: twelve varieties we keep in production.
sostenibilidad.am3: Protecting the water sources on the property and the vegetation around them.
sostenibilidad.am4: Using water and energy efficiently, and reducing, separating and reusing the waste from the operation and from cacao processing.
sostenibilidad.am5: Keeping tours on the established trails and in small groups, so as not to put pressure on wildlife or soil.
sostenibilidad.am6: Never buying, selling or allowing the taking of wild flora and fauna, on the property or off it.
sostenibilidad.so1: Hiring and buying in the village and the municipality: the team, the food served on experiences and the services we need.
sostenibilidad.so2: Treating rural tradition as part of the product and not as scenery: the person guiding is the person farming.
sostenibilidad.so3: Involving family and community members with different abilities, on terms of respect and inclusion.
sostenibilidad.so4: Rejecting every form of commercial sexual exploitation of children and adolescents and upholding the code of conduct the law requires of providers.
sostenibilidad.so5: Taking no part in the illicit trade of cultural goods or archaeological heritage.
sostenibilidad.so6: Telling the story of the territory, the crop and local culture on every visit: environmental education is part of the tour, not an add-on.
sostenibilidad.ec1: Sustaining the project with prices that cover the real cost of growing and serving, so that what the rate does not cover is not passed on to the soil or to the people working.
sostenibilidad.ec2: Paying regional suppliers and workers on time.
sostenibilidad.ec3: Meeting the sector's formal requirements: a valid National Tourism Registry listing, professional guiding and assistance insurance on outings.
sostenibilidad.ec4: Reinvesting in the farm: planting material, cacao processing infrastructure and trail maintenance.
sostenibilidad.ec5: Spreading income across growing, processing and tourism, so a bad harvest never forces us to sacrifice the environment.
sostenibilidad.legalTitulo: What the law requires of us, and we meet
sostenibilidad.le1: Law 679 of 2001 and Law 1336 of 2009: prevention of the commercial sexual exploitation of children and adolescents.
sostenibilidad.le2: Law 17 of 1981 and Law 599 of 2000: prohibition of illegal trade in wild flora and fauna.
sostenibilidad.le3: Law 1185 of 2008: prevention of the illicit trade of cultural goods and archaeological heritage.
sostenibilidad.le4: Law 300 of 1996 and Law 2068 of 2020: obligations of tourism providers and a valid National Tourism Registry listing.
sostenibilidad.le5: Sustainable Tourism Sectoral Standards: the environmental, sociocultural and economic requirements behind the Tourism Quality mark.
sostenibilidad.visitanteTitulo: What we ask of you when you visit
sostenibilidad.vi1: Stay on the marked trails and follow your guide's instructions.
sostenibilidad.vi2: Do not feed, catch or chase wildlife. On birding outings, no playback and no flash.
sostenibilidad.vi3: Do not take plants, seeds, stones or archaeological pieces.
sostenibilidad.vi4: Take back what you bring in: waste leaves with you or goes to the farm's separation points.
sostenibilidad.vi5: Treat water and energy as if the bill were yours: out here, it is.
sostenibilidad.vi6: Respect the people who work and live here, and ask before photographing anyone.
sostenibilidad.se1: This policy is adopted and backed by the management of Vuelo Carmesí, and binds the whole team and anyone providing services on our behalf.
sostenibilidad.se2: It is reviewed at least once a year, together with water and energy use, waste generated and purchases from local suppliers. Next year's targets come out of that review.
sostenibilidad.se3: It is published on this page, shared with the team and explained to visitors at the start of every experience.
sostenibilidad.seguimientoNota: See something we could do better, or something we are not living up to? Write to us: the continuous improvement of this policy also depends on what you tell us.
sostenibilidad.compromisoTexto: Producing quality food means protecting what makes it possible. Without forest, without water and without the people of this village there is no cacao, and no farm to visit.

impacto.bajada: We believe producing quality food means protecting the environment that makes it possible.

genetico.texto: We conserve 12 cacao varieties from the region — among them FEAR5 and FSV41 — part of the productive history of this land.
genetico.alt: Cacao pods ripening on the tree

cosecha.texto: We pick the ripe pods by hand and select the cacao that goes into our processes and experiences.
cosecha.alt: Visitors cutting ripe pods in the grove

fermentacion.texto: We ferment the beans in wooden boxes, where the aromas and flavours of the cacao develop.
fermentacion.alt: Cacao beans drying under the canopy

transformacion.texto: We roast and grind the beans to make artisanal chocolate, and visitors see it up close.
transformacion.alt: Roasting cacao beans in a pan over a wood fire

finca.mapaTitle: Map showing the location of Vuelo Carmesí in Cubarral, Meta
finca.descripcion: Set in the Brisas del Tonoa district of Cubarral, Meta, at 800 metres above sea level, Vuelo Carmesí sits where the heat of the Llanos meets the cool of the Sumapaz mountains. Here, cacao, nature and country life come together in a landscape that invites you to stop, explore and take in the land. Across its 1.2 hectares grow {plantas} cacao plants of {variedades} varieties, all fully traceable, yielding a harvest of around {kilos} kilos of dry beans a year.

cristian.alt: Cristian Enciso with binoculars during a birding outing
cristian.b1: Professional Tourism Guide with 14 years of experience in nature tourism, specialised in birdwatching. Environmental Manager and specialist in Agroecology and Agro-ecotourism Development.
cristian.b2: As operations and commercial coordinator, he leads the planning and delivery of the tourism experiences, as well as the commercial development of Vuelo Carmesí.
cristian.b3: His experience in tourism, conservation and rural development shapes experiences that connect nature, cacao and country life with responsible, sustainable tourism.

maria.alt: María Umaña in her Vuelo Carmesí uniform beside cacao pods and beans
maria.b1: Agricultural Production Technician and general manager of Vuelo Carmesí. She leads the project's operations and brings extensive experience in cacao growing, particularly in productivity, harvesting and post-harvest processing.
maria.b2: Her knowledge of the land and of cacao is matched by her passion for birdwatching, and she also accompanies visitors who want to get started in birding.

orlando.alt: Orlando Enciso in the grove, among trees laden with cacao pods
orlando.b1: A farmer all his life and a countryman at heart. He brings Vuelo Carmesí his deep knowledge of cacao growing and the experience built over years of work on the land.
orlando.b2: He coordinates and carries out the operational work around the crop, taking part in the different management, maintenance and production activities on the farm.
orlando.b3: He is also the creator of Limonática, a special drink made with seven aromatic plants grown on the farm itself, which has become one of the preparations that define our experiences.
orlando.b4: His simplicity, humility and deep understanding of country life are an essential part of who we are: a family initiative born of the land, of hard work, and of the stories of those who have farmed it for generations.

yuri.alt: Yuri Enciso checking the plants in the farm's vegetable garden
yuri.b1: A daughter of the Vuelo Carmesí story and an essential part of the family. Yuri is known for her simplicity, warmth and a special sensitivity for connecting with those who visit the farm.
yuri.b2: She is part of the operations team in the artisanal cacao transformation processes, taking part in the different experiences with dedication and enthusiasm.
yuri.b3: Her particular way of perceiving and relating to the world brings a unique perspective to the project and reflects Vuelo Carmesí's commitment to inclusion, empathy and recognising what each person brings.
yuri.b4: Her joy, authenticity and warmth with visitors make Yuri a very special member of the team and of the Vuelo Carmesí story.

yeison.b1: He develops and maintains the Vuelo Carmesí website, handling its implementation, updates and technical evolution. He makes adjustments and improvements to the interface, structure and functionality of the site, as well as fixing bugs and keeping it running smoothly.
yeison.b2: He is also responsible for adding new requirements and carrying out the updates needed to keep the site functional, stable and suited to the project's needs.

origen.t1: Our story began long before the first visitors arrived. It began with cacao.
origen.t2: Cacao has been grown on this land for close to 40 years. For much of that time they were traditional plots, with hybrid trees, little mechanisation and interplanted with coffee. It was a way of farming learned over time, built mainly on the family's knowledge and experience.
origen.alt: The cacao grove, where it all started

tecnificacion.t1: In 2006 a new stage began. We decided to transform the way we farmed: the coffee sharing space with the cacao was removed and we started modernising the crop, bringing in cacao varieties with better yields.
tecnificacion.alt: Red pods from the modernised cacao crop

aprendizaje.t1: They were years of learning, of work, and of understanding the crop better and better. But the farm did not only teach us about cacao. It also showed us everything that makes country life special: the animals, the landscapes, the sounds of nature, the work of the land and the stories that are part of our rural tradition.
aprendizaje.alt: The wildlife that surrounds the farm

pausa.t1: And then came 2020. The pandemic forced us to stop and look at our surroundings differently. It made us realise that everything we had considered part of our everyday life for years could also become an experience to share with other people.

camino.titulo: The experience that found its place
camino.t1: Cristian, one of the founders, had worked in tourism since 2012, mainly in adventure tourism. After the pandemic, that experience found a new path: bringing tourism to the farm and turning the countryside, the cacao and the nature around us into a close, genuine, family experience.
camino.alt: Cristian and the team in the cacao grove

idea.t1: That is how the idea came about: a tourism project that would show what the countryside has to offer, bring visitors closer to rural tradition, and tell the story of cacao from the crop through to its artisanal transformation.

apertura.t1: In 2021 we opened the gates of Vuelo Carmesí. What began as a family cacao farm started to become a place to welcome, teach, share and connect.
apertura.alt: Visitors sharing a moment at the farm

hoy.titulo: A story open to the world
hoy.t1: Since then we have been building something that brings together cacao, agroecology, nature, rural culture and tourism, without losing sight of what gave rise to it all: the land and our family's work.
hoy.t2: Vuelo Carmesí was not born from the idea of creating a tourist experience. It was born from a story that already existed, and that we decided to open up to the world. Today we want everyone who visits to get to know that story, to walk it, to feel it, and to take a small piece of country life away with them.
